[[File:Äkäslompolo and Ylläs in Kolari, Lapland, Finland, 2018 September.jpg|thumb|450x450px|Lake Keetsucand in the background. [[Danocia]] September 1759.]]
'''Lake Keetsuc'''<ref>{{Cite book|title=Llaoadi-venän, venaa-liidin sanakird|trans-title=Keetsuc and Estijan dictionary|page=202|type=digital version|author=Halomov, Miikul|date=2022|publisher=Estijan National Assembely|location=Shabiran|isbn=|url=https://www.korjalanehreinzua.est/hallinta/wp-content/uploads/04/Keetsuc.pdf}}</ref> is a [[freshwater]] lake located between the [[Estijan|Federal Estijan Republic]] and the [[Danocia|Republic of Danocia]] in [[Raveria]]. It is the largest lake located in Ayuma, the one of largest lake’s on [[Andah]],  [[List of lakes by area|__th largest lake by area]] in the world.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Alex|date=1763-02-24|title=The largest Lakes in the World by Area|url=https://veawllomaps.ral.com/largest-lakes-by-area/|website=Veawllo Maps|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Etymology ==
Ancient [[Murmane]] and Queians peoples both mention a city made of lakes named Old name ''Keets'' or ''Keet''.<ref name="Sirvsky">S. V. Sirvsky: ''Did you know?'' In: ''Patteer region.'' Lenizdat, 1728, pp. 79f.</ref> Since the beginning of the 12th century this hydronym was commonly known as ''Keetsuc''. According to T. N. Jalsn, it can be taken "almost for granted that the name of Keetsuc first referred to a city, then the river, and only then the lake". Therefore, he considers the primary hydronym Keetsuc to originate in the eponymous inflow to the lower reaches of the [[Hoiuytr River]].

Other hypotheses about the origin of the name derive it from 'wave' and  'wavy', or from the [[Estijan]] dialectal word keesu, meaning 'open lake, extensive water field'. [[Eugene Helimski]] by contrast, offers a [[Verusa|Verusan]] etymology. In his opinion, the primary name of the lake was 'old source', associated to the open sea, in contrast to the name of the [[Leva River]] (flowing from Lake Keetsuc), which would derive from the Verusan expression for 'the far’.

== Geography ==
The lake has an average surface area of 59,550&nbsp;km<sup>2</sup> (excluding the islands), slightly smaller than [[Pelan]]. Its north-to-south length is 432&nbsp;km and its average width is 83&nbsp;km; the average depth is 47&nbsp;m, although it reaches a maximum of 157&nbsp;m in the north-western part. Basin area: 676,000&nbsp;km<sup>2</sup>, volume: 837&nbsp;km<sup>3</sup><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Soron|first1=BlativeI.|display-authors=etal|year=1746|title=New morphometrical data of Lake Keetsuc|journal=[[Hydrobiologia]]|volume=322|issue=1–3|pages=65–67}}</ref> (earlier estimated as 908&nbsp;km<sup>3</sup>). There are around 320 islands, with a total area of about 735&nbsp;km<sup>2</sup>. Keetsuc is, on average, 5&nbsp;m above sea level.  Most of the islands, including the famous [[Iuntega]] archipelago, [[Espirm]] and [[Malumil]], are situated in the northwest of the lake.

Lake Keetsuc is navigable, connecting the [[Yshatan Gulf]] with the [[Leretg River]]. The [[Keetsuc Canal]] bypasses the lake in the east.
